question: Which sequence best represents the usual high-level software life cycle?

options.text: Requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, maintenance
Design, maintenance, requirements, deployment, implementation, testing
Implementation, requirements, testing, design, maintenance, deployment
Testing, implementation, deployment, requirements, design, maintenance

explanation: A typical life cycle moves from understanding requirements through design and implementation to verification, delivery, and ongoing maintenance; specific models may organize or repeat these activities differently.

question: A team begins coding before clarifying important user needs. Later, major features must be redesigned. Which SDLC activity was most clearly inadequate?
explanation: Requirements analysis identifies and clarifies what stakeholders need before design and implementation depend on those decisions.

question: Which activity primarily converts approved requirements into the structure, components, interfaces, and data organization of a solution?
explanation: Design defines how the system will be structured and how its parts will realize the requirements.

question: A developer translates a module's design into source code and checks syntax and basic execution. Which SDLC phase is primarily involved?
explanation: Implementation converts design specifications into executable code.

question: After deployment, a government rule changes and the application must be updated to remain compliant. Which life-cycle activity handles this change?
explanation: Maintenance includes adapting software to changed external conditions, including new regulations.

question: Which statement about SDLC is most accurate?

options.text: Every SDLC model uses exactly the same sequence with no iteration
SDLC describes organized activities used to develop and maintain software
SDLC begins only after source code has been written
SDLC refers only to testing and deployment

explanation: SDLC organizes software development and maintenance activities; different process models arrange and revisit them differently.

question: A team performs requirements, design, coding, and testing in small repeated cycles, delivering usable increments after each cycle. Which statement best describes this approach?

options.text: The life cycle can be iterative and incremental
The life cycle must be strictly one-pass and sequential
Maintenance must finish before implementation begins
Testing is excluded until the entire product is retired

explanation: Iterative development revisits activities; incremental development delivers the product in successive usable portions.

question: Which of the following is generally considered an umbrella activity rather than a phase performed only once?

options.text: Software quality assurance throughout the project
Writing the first version of a single module

explanation: Umbrella activities, such as quality assurance, risk management, measurement, and configuration management, span multiple life-cycle activities.

question: A project tracks risks, manages changes, measures progress, and conducts quality reviews during requirements, design, coding, and testing. These are best classified as:

options.text: Umbrella activities supporting the life cycle
Activities restricted to the coding phase
Deployment tasks that begin after acceptance
Maintenance tasks that cannot occur during development

explanation: Risk management, software quality assurance, configuration management, and project tracking commonly continue across the life cycle.

question: Which activity is most directly concerned with determining whether a proposed software project is technically, economically, and operationally feasible?
explanation: A feasibility study evaluates whether the proposed solution is practical and worthwhile under relevant constraints.

question: In a project, a stakeholder confirms that the delivered system supports the intended business tasks and satisfies agreed needs. Which activity is most directly represented?
explanation: Validation asks whether the product meets user needs; acceptance testing often provides evidence for stakeholder acceptance.

question: Which statement best distinguishes verification from validation in the SDLC?

options.text: Verification checks conformance to specified requirements; validation checks whether the product meets user needs
Verification occurs only after release; validation occurs only before design
Verification checks usability only; validation checks source-code syntax only
Verification and validation are identical terms for compiling code

explanation: Verification evaluates whether work products meet specifications; validation evaluates whether the resulting product is the right one for users.

question: A team tests each module separately before combining the modules into a complete application. Which testing level is being used first?
explanation: Unit testing checks individual components or modules in isolation before broader integration and system testing.

question: A project has passed module-level tests, but data is incorrectly passed between two modules when they are combined. Which activity is most directly intended to uncover such problems?
explanation: Integration testing focuses on interactions and interfaces among combined components.

question: Which sequence is most appropriate when a team follows a traditional staged process with formal phase completion and approval before the next phase begins?
explanation: A staged process commonly moves from requirements to design, implementation, testing, and deployment, though real projects may revisit earlier work.

question: Which limitation is most commonly associated with a strict Waterfall-style process when requirements change substantially late in development?

options.text: Revisiting completed phases can be costly and disruptive
It cannot produce any written documentation
It requires every feature to be released daily
It eliminates the need for requirements analysis

explanation: Waterfall emphasizes staged progression, so substantial late changes may require costly rework in earlier phases.

question: Which statement about the Spiral model is most accurate?

options.text: Each cycle emphasizes identifying and addressing risks before committing to further development
It prohibits prototyping and risk analysis
It requires all requirements to remain unchanged from the beginning
It is simply a name for testing after coding

explanation: The Spiral model is risk-driven; each loop typically includes objective setting, risk analysis, development/validation, and planning the next cycle.

question: A project has major technical uncertainties and a high cost of failure. The team wants to evaluate risks and prototypes in repeated cycles before committing fully. Which model is the strongest fit?
explanation: The Spiral model is especially suited to risk-intensive projects because risk analysis guides each development cycle.

question: A team builds a quick working version so users can clarify poorly understood requirements before the final product is engineered. Which approach is being used?
explanation: Prototyping uses an early model to obtain feedback and clarify requirements or design choices.

question: Which risk can arise if a quick prototype is repeatedly patched and then treated as production software without suitable redesign?

options.text: Prototype shortcuts may leave a weak architecture and difficult-to-maintain code
User feedback becomes impossible to collect
Requirements automatically become complete and stable
All testing becomes unnecessary because users saw the prototype

explanation: A prototype may prioritize learning and speed over robust architecture; turning it directly into a product can preserve shortcuts and technical weaknesses.

question: Which model explicitly organizes development into a sequence of stages and commonly associates each development stage with a corresponding testing stage?
explanation: The V-Model links development activities with corresponding test levels, emphasizing test planning and verification/validation relationships.

question: In the V-Model, system requirements are most directly associated with planning which corresponding test level?
explanation: In the common V-Model mapping, user or system requirements correspond to acceptance testing; architecture and detailed design map to lower test levels.

question: A product is delivered in several planned releases, each adding a useful subset of functionality. Which development characteristic is most clearly present?

options.text: Single final delivery with no intermediate builds
Maintenance before any working software exists
Testing limited to the first release

explanation: Incremental development builds and delivers functionality in successive portions rather than waiting for one complete final release.

question: What is the key distinction between iterative and incremental development?

options.text: Iteration refines the solution through repeated cycles; increments add usable pieces of functionality
Iteration means adding features only; increment means repeating the same phase only
Iteration is limited to testing; increments are limited to requirements
They are always mutually exclusive and cannot be combined

explanation: Iteration emphasizes refinement through repetition, while increment emphasizes staged addition of functionality; a project can use both.

question: Which statement best describes the CMMI maturity-level sequence for staged representation?

options.text: Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimizing
Managed, Initial, Defined, Optimizing, Quantitatively Managed
Initial, Defined, Managed, Optimizing, Quantitatively Managed
Defined, Initial, Managed, Quantitatively Managed, Optimizing

explanation: The five staged CMMI maturity levels are Level 1 Initial, Level 2 Managed, Level 3 Defined, Level 4 Quantitatively Managed, and Level 5 Optimizing.

question: An organization has unpredictable processes that depend heavily on individual effort, with little consistent project control. Which CMMI maturity level best describes this situation?
explanation: At Initial maturity, processes are often ad hoc or unpredictable and success may depend on individual effort.

question: A company establishes project-level planning, monitoring, and control so that commitments are managed and work products are tracked. Which CMMI maturity level is the best match?
explanation: Managed processes are planned, monitored, and controlled at the project level.

question: A software organization defines and standardizes a common process across projects, allowing teams to tailor it under established guidelines. Which CMMI level best fits?
explanation: Defined maturity means organizational processes are documented, standardized, and tailored for individual projects as appropriate.

question: An organization uses statistical and quantitative techniques to control process performance and determine whether process objectives are being met. Which CMMI level is most directly indicated?
explanation: Quantitatively Managed focuses on controlling process performance using quantitative objectives and measurement.

question: A mature organization systematically improves its processes using quantitative feedback, root-cause analysis, and innovation. Which CMMI maturity level best matches this emphasis?
explanation: Optimizing maturity emphasizes continuous process improvement, including innovation and analysis of causes of variation or defects.

question: Which CMMI maturity level comes immediately after Defined in the five-level staged representation?
explanation: The sequence is Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, and Optimizing.

question: A team uses a board with columns such as To Do, In Progress, and Done, limits work in progress, and continuously pulls the next task when capacity becomes available. Which approach is most directly described?
explanation: Kanban visualizes workflow, limits work in progress, and supports a continuous flow of work.

question: Which statement about Scrum is correct?

options.text: Work is organized into time-boxed Sprints, with defined accountabilities and inspect-and-adapt events
All requirements must be fully frozen before any Sprint can begin
Scrum prohibits review of working product until the final release
Scrum requires every task to be completed by one individual only

explanation: Scrum uses Sprints and defined accountabilities, events, and artifacts to support transparency, inspection, and adaptation.

question: In Scrum, which artifact contains the ordered list of work needed to improve the product and serves as the single source of work for the Scrum Team?
explanation: The Product Backlog is the ordered, evolving list of work needed to improve the product.

question: Which statement best reflects the Agile Manifesto's emphasis?

options.text: Individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change are valued
Comprehensive documentation and contract negotiation are valued above all alternatives
Following a fixed plan is valued over responding to changing circumstances
Tools and processes replace the need for communication with customers

explanation: The Agile Manifesto values individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change, while still valuing the items on the right.

question: A team delivers small working releases frequently, invites customer feedback, and adjusts its backlog as needs change. Which approach does this most strongly reflect?
explanation: Frequent delivery, collaboration, feedback, and adaptation are central characteristics of Agile approaches.

question: Which practice is most closely associated with Extreme Programming (XP)?

options.text: Avoiding automated tests until the product is complete
Freezing all requirements before the first iteration
Separating developers so that code is never reviewed

explanation: XP promotes engineering practices such as pair programming, test-driven development, continuous integration, and frequent small releases.

question: A team wants to shorten feedback cycles by integrating code changes frequently and running automated builds and tests. Which practice is most directly relevant?
explanation: Continuous integration merges changes frequently and validates them with automated builds and tests to detect integration problems early.

question: A software team has a stable, well-understood project with clearly specified requirements and formal approval gates. Which process model may be reasonable if changes are expected to be limited?

options.text: Risk-driven Spiral model in every case
Prototype-only model with no final engineering

explanation: Waterfall can suit projects with relatively stable requirements and a need for staged documentation and approvals, though no model fits every project.

question: A system's most important uncertainty is whether users can operate a proposed interface. The team creates a low-cost mock-up and asks representative users to try it before finalizing the design. What is the main purpose?

options.text: Reduce uncertainty and refine requirements or design through feedback
Prove that the final system has no defects
Replace all later integration and system testing
Establish the final production architecture without further analysis

explanation: Prototypes help explore uncertain requirements and design choices by gathering early feedback; they do not prove the finished product defect-free.

question: Which activity is most directly concerned with tracking whether actual project work is progressing according to planned schedule and effort?
explanation: Project monitoring and control compares actual progress with plans and supports corrective action when deviations occur.

question: Which statement about documentation in the SDLC is most accurate?

options.text: Documentation can support communication, traceability, maintenance, and compliance when appropriate to project needs
Documentation is useful only after software has been retired
Documentation makes testing and stakeholder communication unnecessary

explanation: Documentation supports communication and future work; Agile values working software but does not prohibit useful documentation.

question: A team changes a requirement during development. It records the change, assesses its impact on design and tests, and obtains approval before implementation. Which supporting activity is most directly involved?
explanation: Change management evaluates, approves, records, and tracks changes to controlled requirements and other work products.

question: Which of the following is NOT normally an SDLC phase or life-cycle activity?

options.text: CPU instruction decoding by the processor

explanation: CPU instruction decoding is a processor operation, not a software development life-cycle activity.

question: A product is released, and the team continues fixing defects, improving performance, and adapting it to a new operating environment. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Maintenance can include corrective, perfective, and adaptive changes after delivery
Maintenance means only correcting syntax errors before the first release
Once deployed, the product is outside the software life cycle
Performance improvement is never considered software maintenance

explanation: Post-delivery maintenance includes correcting faults, adapting to environmental changes, and improving performance or other qualities.

question: Which pairing is most accurate?

options.text: Alpha testing—typically conducted at the developer's site; Beta testing—evaluated by selected users in a real or user environment
Alpha testing—performed only by the compiler; Beta testing—performed only by the database
Alpha testing—after retirement; Beta testing—before requirements are collected
Alpha testing—only unit testing; Beta testing—only code review

explanation: In common usage, alpha testing occurs in a controlled developer environment, while beta testing involves selected external users or a user environment before wider release.

question: Which statement about a software process model is most accurate?

options.text: It provides an organized framework for carrying out life-cycle activities
It is a programming language used to implement requirements
It guarantees that a project will finish within budget
It replaces the need to understand stakeholder requirements

explanation: A process model organizes and guides life-cycle activities; choosing a model cannot by itself guarantee project success.

question: A project team discovers that a design assumption is invalid during implementation. Which response is most consistent with sound SDLC practice?

options.text: Review the affected design and requirements, assess impacts, and revise controlled work products as needed
Ignore the issue because design must never be revisited
Delete the requirements so the implementation can continue
Release immediately and let users discover the impact

explanation: A disciplined life cycle allows justified feedback and rework while managing changes and preserving traceability.

question: Which option best describes the purpose of software quality assurance as an umbrella activity?

options.text: To provide planned activities that help processes and work products conform to applicable quality requirements
To test only the user interface after deployment
To replace project planning with defect counting
To guarantee that no defect can ever occur

explanation: SQA spans the project and helps provide confidence that processes and products follow applicable standards and requirements; it cannot guarantee zero defects.

question: A company uses CMMI to improve how it develops software. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.text: CMMI provides a framework for assessing and improving process capability or maturity
CMMI is a software testing technique used only on individual functions
CMMI is a programming language for writing process models
CMMI specifies one mandatory SDLC model for every project

explanation: CMMI is a process-improvement framework; it does not prescribe one universal development model for every project.
